passage:
Tuesday night, 11 pm. Today Wasim solved the maths problem that had stumped me, and I felt irritated, not impressed. I actually thought the words "scholarship kid" in my head. At the canteen I took the bench he was heading for and pretended not to see. When Rakesh joked about Wasim wearing the same shoes all term, I laughed too.
Now I can't sleep. My driver drops me at the gate each morning. Wasim takes two buses and still turns in every worksheet. I have a tutor; he has a library card, and he beat me anyway.
Tomorrow I'm going to ask him how he solved it, and mean it.
Suraj

qa.q: How does Wasim get to school?
What was Suraj feeling when Wasim solved the maths problem, and what does Suraj feel later?
qa.a: Suraj was irritated rather than impressed, and by night feels uneasy about the thought, 'scholarship kid', and about laughing along.

qa.q: What could Suraj do differently tomorrow?
qa.a: Suraj could ask Wasim how he solved the problem and truly listen, treating Wasim as a classmate for who he is.

qa.q: How might Wasim have felt when Suraj took the bench and others joked about his shoes?
qa.a: Wasim probably felt left out and judged before anyone knew him, even though he works hard and turns in every worksheet.

grounding: A well-off teen notices their contempt for a scholarship classmate, sees how privilege shapes them, and resolves to treat the classmate as a person.
